title: Introduce invocation signal concierge and token lifecycle map
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds an invocation-level signal orchestration service (Signal Concierge), a token lifecycle mapping exporter, two dashboards and tuned alert presets for long-tail token cost/latency anomalies.
description:
Context and motivation: Production teams asked for finer-grained attribution when investigating long-tail cost/latency regressions where standard per-invocation traces lacked lifecycle semantics (e.g., token-level warmups, kv-cache rehydration, cross-stage retries). This PR introduces a lightweight service we call Signal Concierge that assembles invocation signals (metrics, spans, sparse logs) into a compact token lifecycle map and exports a compact lineage artifact that can be consumed by dashboards and our alerting pipeline. The goal is to reduce MTTR by making the token-level transitions visible and by surfacing cost/latency contributors across model stages and kernel boundaries.

What this changes (high level): 
- Add service: telemetry/signal-concierge (golang) that consumes sampled spans, metric events and curated logs; correlates by invocation-id and produces a token_lifecycle artifact per invocation. The artifact contains per-token phase tags (init, kv_warmup, model_step, streaming_emit), aggregated phase durations, and cost-estimates.
- Exporter: observability/exporters/token-life-writer -> writes compressed artifacts to object storage + index in query-store.
- Dashboards: two new Grafana panels added: "Token Lifecycle Trace" (per-invocation token phase timeline) and "Token Phase Cost Waterfall" (aggregated across cohorts).
- Alerts: add tuned alert rules that detect spikes in phase-specific p95/p99 (e.g., kv_warmup p99 increase), and an alert softening policy that debounces on transient spikes using the existing alert-orchestrator.
- SDK: small additions to trace-enricher to emit phase hints for streaming responses.

Operational notes and rollout plan: 
- Feature gated behind `obs.signal_concierge` and `obs.token_lifecycle_export` toggles.
- Canary rollout: enable for internal orgs first (devops + platform), then roll to 10% of tenant traffic, monitor token-lifecycle artifact volume and ultimate storage costs for 48h.
- If artifact rate exceeds 500/s, concierge reduces sampling rate by drop policy with priority for SLO failing invocations.
- Runbook: added short remediation steps to Grafana dashboard (link) and a playbook in infra/runbooks/token_lifecycle_playbook.md describing how to silence phase alerts and temporarily disable artifact writes.

Security & privacy: 
- Token lifecycle artifacts do not contain raw user text. Phase hints are metadata-only; any identifiers are hashed with tenant-scoped salt. The compliance review confirmed artifacts are safe for object-store retention under existing retention policies.

Metrics and expected impact: 
- New metrics emitted: signal_concierge.processed_invocations, token_life.artifact_size_bytes, token_life.truncated_invocations, token_phase.{init,kv_warmup,model_step,streaming_emit}.duration_ms (p50/p95/p99 summaries)
- Expected operational wins: reduce MTTR for kv-warmup regressions by ~40% (observed in internal replaybench), and enable faster alert triage by surfacing which token phase dominates cost.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main. Post-merge actions: feature flags set to internal orgs; nightly e2e job scheduled; billing impact review scheduled in two weeks.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the token_lifecycle artifact compact and time-bounded to avoid runaway storage. We considered embedding the artifacts in traces but opted for a separate artifact to keep trace payloads small and let dashboards consume trimmed, pre-aggregated views.
